South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 08/30/28 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD exacerbation, evaluation of persistent bilateral lower extremity edema, and reassessment of mental health status.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for follow-up approximately six weeks after his last visit. He reports a significant exacerbation of his chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), characterized by increased shortness of breath, particularly during activities of daily living, and frequent nighttime awakenings due to respiratory distress. He states that he has been utilizing his albuterol inhaler up to six times daily, indicating a marked increase in his reliance on rescue medication. The patient also notes that he has experienced a persistent cough with minimal clear sputum production.
The bilateral lower extremity edema continues to be a troubling issue. Mr. Fairfax describes the swelling as worsening, particularly in the evenings, rating the discomfort as an 8/10 on the pain scale. He has been adhering to dietary sodium restrictions, yet the edema has not improved, leading to increased difficulty with ambulation and activities of daily living.
In terms of mental health, Mr. Fairfax reports ongoing feelings of anxiety and sadness, exacerbated by the recent passing of a close friend. He expresses frustration with his current coping mechanisms, stating that he feels overwhelmed and has had difficulty engaging in his usual activities. He mentions that his sleep remains disrupted, with frequent awakenings and difficulty returning to sleep.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + increased fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + increased dyspnea, + cough, + wheezing, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain, + worsening bilateral lower extremity edema. Neurological - + increased anxiety, + insomnia, no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, currently using six times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 2 puffs twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 160 mg daily (no change). 7. Sertraline 150 mg daily (no change).
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.7F, HR 80, BP 132/86, RR 24, O2 sat 78% on room air.
General: Elderly male in moderate respiratory distress, appears fatigued and anxious. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, moderate wheezing noted on expiration, mild crackles at the bases. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 4+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 9.5, Hgb 9.8, Hct 28.5, Plt 210. 2. BMP: Na 128, K 4.2, Cl 95, CO2 22, BUN 45, Cr 2.8, Glucose 90. 3. BNP: 720 (increased). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 2.6 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD exacerbation: Mr. Fairfax's respiratory symptoms have worsened significantly. He will be started on a course of oral prednisone 40 mg daily for 5 days to manage the exacerbation. A follow-up pulmonary function test will be scheduled in one month. Consideration for a referral to pulmonary for further evaluation of his COPD management is warranted if no improvement is noted. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Monitor blood pressure closely given the recent changes in renal function. Follow-up in 1 month. 3. Lower extremity edema: The edema persists despite furosemide therapy. A referral to nephrology will be pursued for further evaluation of renal function and optimization of diuretic therapy. Reinforce dietary sodium restrictions and encourage daily weight monitoring. 4. Mental health: Due to the exacerbation of anxiety and depressive symptoms, Mr. Fairfax will continue with sertraline at 150 mg daily. A follow-up with psychiatry is scheduled in two weeks for ongoing management and reassessment of treatment efficacy. Explore additional therapeutic options such as cognitive-behavioral therapy to address anxiety and insomnia.
Patient education reiterated regarding the importance of recognizing exacerbation signs, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
